title: mcp-sec-bench scanner label mapping
description: One file per scanner. Maps that scanner's own output vocabulary onto the classes in docs/taxonomy.md, or records an explicit refusal to map. Every entry is a judgment call that a vendor may contest under docs/governance.md#contesting-a-result, so every entry carries its reasoning, its author, its date, and -- when contested -- both positions.

scanner_id.description: Must equal the adapter's scanner_id and the scoreboard row key.

display_name.description: Vendor/product name as the vendor writes it.

scanner_versions.description: Scanner versions whose output vocabulary this file was checked against. A label table is only as valid as the versions it was read from.

adapter_version.description: Adapter version whose RawFinding.raw_label this table is keyed on. Changing which field the adapter puts in raw_label invalidates this table.

label_provenance.description: captured-from-real-output: every raw_label below was copied verbatim from output this project actually produced, and the capture is committed. illustrative-placeholder: the labels are invented to demonstrate the format and MUST NOT be used to score anything. unverified: labels taken from vendor docs or a third party but not yet observed in output we ran.

provenance_note.description: Where the labels came from: the committed raw-output path, the docs URL, or the reason they are still placeholders.

label_source_field.description: Which field of the scanner's output the adapter copies into RawFinding.raw_label (e.g. 'rule_id', 'check.name', 'category'). Reviewers cannot check a mapping without knowing what was matched on.

frozen_for_corpus_version.description: The corpus_version this table was frozen against before a scoring run, per docs/scoring.md. Null while the table is still being drafted.

matching.description: The ONLY normalization the mapping layer may apply. Both default to false, i.e. byte-exact matching. Nothing else is permitted: fuzzy, stemmed, or substring matching would make a table unreviewable and would let the mapping layer manufacture credit.

case_insensitive.description: Unicode casefold both sides before comparing. Only set true for a scanner whose output genuinely varies in case between runs or versions; say so in `note`.

strip_surrounding_whitespace.description: Strip leading/trailing whitespace from the observed label before comparing. Interior whitespace is never touched.

note.description: Required in review practice whenever either flag is true: the observed instability that justifies it.

notes.description: File-level remarks: vocabulary quirks, engines whose labels are not covered, known gaps.

entries.description: One entry per raw label. Entries are keyed on (raw_label, applies_to_stage); duplicates are a load error.

then.description: A placeholder file must mark every entry illustrative, so no real run can be scored against invented labels by accident.

rationale_id.description: Stable identifier, convention MR-<scanner_id>-<NNN>. Written into every MappedFinding and into results JSON as mapping_rationale_id, and cited in docs/mapping-rationale.md. Never reused, never renumbered: a published number points at it.

raw_label.description: The scanner's label, VERBATIM, exactly as it appears in the field named by label_source_field. Never cleaned up, never re-cased, never re-spaced.

label_note.description: What the scanner means by this label, in the vendor's own terms where they document it.

applies_to_stage.description: Scope the entry to findings produced in one stage. The ONLY permitted way to give a single raw label two different mappings, because stage is a hard fact the runner records rather than a judgment about the finding's text. Used when a scanner's one label covers a metadata payload found by source scanning (A1) and a return-value payload found by exercising the server (A4). Two entries sharing a raw_label must have disjoint stage scopes.

decision.description: Explicit, so that 'no class' is always a recorded decision and never a missing field. `unmapped` costs the scanner nothing (docs/scoring.md#normalization).

mapped_class.description: The class this label is credited as. Null exactly when decision is `unmapped`.

unmapped_reason.description: Why we decline to map. `insufficient-specificity` and `no-defensible-single-class` are the honest answers when a label is real but too coarse to place; they are a finding about OUR taxonomy, not about the scanner.

taxonomy_evidence.description: Required for every `map` decision. A mapping is only defensible if it cites the class's present-when test in docs/taxonomy.md and says how the scanner's label satisfies it.

present_when_quote.description: The present-when text from docs/taxonomy.md for mapped_class, quoted.

why_satisfied.description: How what this label reports satisfies that test.

considered_classes.description: Every other class whose present-when test this label plausibly satisfies, and why it lost. Present on any label that spans classes -- the spanning is the interesting part and must not be hidden by a single-line table row.

resolution_rules.description: Which rules of the decision procedure in docs/mapping-rationale.md were applied. Required whenever considered_classes is present.

rationale.description: The prose a disputing vendor argues with. Written to be read by someone who disagrees.

confidence.description: high: the label and the class name the same property. medium: a defensible reading with a rejected alternative. low: we picked one of several readings and expect to be argued with.

dispute_risk.description: Our own estimate of how likely this entry is to be contested. Published, so the invitation to contest is not buried.

status.description: provisional: drafted before the label was seen in real output. disputed: contested under governance.md and not resolved in our favour by agreement. withdrawn: superseded; kept because published results are never silently edited.

illustrative.description: True means this label is INVENTED to demonstrate the format. The loader refuses to score with it unless explicitly asked to.

decided_by.description: Who made the call. A maintainer with a disclosed tie to this scanner must recuse (governance.md#conflicts-of-interest).

dispute.description: The both-positions record required by governance.md#contesting-a-result. When we are not persuaded, the vendor's position is published on the scoreboard row beside ours rather than replaced by our resolution of it.

forum.description: Public issue or PR reference. Disputes are never resolved privately.

vendor_position.description: The disputing party's argument, in their words, unedited except for length.

vendor_proposed_class.description: The class they say this label should map to; null if they say it should be unmapped.

our_position.description: Why we hold the mapping, answering their argument rather than restating ours.

outcome.description: mapping-changed: we were persuaded; the entry above already reflects their reading and history records the change. both-positions-published: we were not persuaded; both readings go on the scoreboard row.

scoreboard_note.description: The short both-positions text rendered on the scoreboard row.

affected_items.description: server/class items whose outcome changes if the vendor's reading is applied. Makes the stake of the dispute concrete.

redisclosure_sent_on.description: A mapping change affecting a published score triggers a published correction notice (governance.md#publication-and-right-of-reply). Field name kept from the earlier pre-publication disclosure policy.

history.description: Every change to this entry after it was first published. Published results are never silently edited.
